prompt: Implement the provided SimpleStack interface in the ListStack class using an ArrayList: push adds, pop removes and returns the most recently pushed element (null when empty), and isEmpty reports whether the stack is empty.
explanation: An interface says WHAT operations exist; the implementing class decides HOW. Here an ArrayList works as stack storage by always adding and removing at the end (index size() - 1), which makes both operations fast and gives LIFO order. Guarding pop() with an isEmpty check turns the would-be IndexOutOfBoundsException into the interface's documented null result.
hints: push is one line: items.add(s); -- adding at the end makes the end the top of the stack.
In pop(), first return null if items.isEmpty(); otherwise remove the element at index items.size() - 1.
ArrayList already has an isEmpty() method you can delegate to.
